title: inbox: a session reads its DMs, its items' threads and its channel by cursor

story.i_want_to: read everything addressed to me (my DMs, the threads of the items I hold, my repo's channel) from where I last stopped, and mark it read only when I have it
story.so_that: nothing is skipped, nothing is read twice, and an item I take over arrives with its whole thread

rationale: PRD R11: every session has exactly one inbox (its DMs plus the threads of the items it holds), read by a cursor kept per attachment, and a holder that takes an item over starts that thread at its beginning. Today the only reads are channel_recent (Coordination.recent_page/3, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:3550), newest-first with a 5 s look-back that re-delivers on purpose and leaves exact-once dedup to the client (:256-281), and channel_get. No read is per session, and no cursor is stored on the server: the existing Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelCursor (lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_cursor.ex:1) is an opaque keyset-paging token, not a stored read position, so it cannot serve; the stored cursor is a new table.

acceptance_criteria.description: A table channel_cursors (tenant_id, holder_id FK holders ON DELETE CASCADE, attachment_kind dm | story | channel, attachment_id, last_seq bigint default 0, timestamps), RLS enabled, schema Loopctl.Coordination.InboxCursor, with the unique index channel_cursors_holder_attachment_uidx on (holder_id, attachment_kind, attachment_id).

Messages.inbox/3 (tenant_id, holder_id, opts) returns, for each attachment of the holder's inbox (its own DMs, the thread of every story whose assigned_holder_id is the holder, and the channel of opts[:project_id] when given), the messages with attachment_seq above that attachment's last_seq in ascending order, at most opts[:limit] in total (default 50, clamped to 200) with has_more, and moves no cursor.

Messages.ack/3 (tenant_id, holder_id, [%{kind, id, seq}]) sets each cursor's last_seq to the greater of its current value and seq, creating the row when absent; a seq above the attachment's highest attachment_seq answers {:error, {:ack_beyond_end, kind, id}}, and an attachment outside the holder's inbox answers {:error, {:not_in_inbox, kind, id}}, with no cursor changed by a refused call.

A holder that becomes a story's assigned holder (a claim or a takeover) has no cursor on that thread, so its next inbox read returns the thread from attachment_seq 1, and the previous holder's cursor neither moves nor is read.

GET /api/v1/inbox (project_id, limit) and POST /api/v1/inbox/ack ({acks: [...]}) need a holder credential (role: :agent with a holder_id): any other key answers 403 code holder_credential_required; the response groups messages as {dms, threads: [{story_id, messages}], channel} with each attachment's highest returned seq.

The MCP tool inbox takes optional project_id, limit and ack; with ack it posts the acks first and then reads, and its description says the cursor moves only on ack, so an unacked message is returned again.
A message that commits on an attachment after a read and before its ack is returned by the next read: an ack carries the seq the caller last received, never the attachment's current end.
Projects.Merge.merge_into/4 deletes the channel cursors whose attachment_id is the source project, so a holder reads the merged channel from its start once.

test_cases.name: inbox gathers DMs, held threads and the channel past each cursor (DataCase)
preconditions: holder H (fixture(:holder), US-52.13); stories S1 held by H (assigned_holder_id, US-52.14) and S2 held by another holder; 2 DMs to H, 3 messages on S1, 1 on S2, 2 on the channel
expected_results: first: 2 dms, S1's 3 in seq order, 2 channel, nothing from S2; second: no channel section; neither call writes a channel_cursors row

test_cases.name: limit and has_more (DataCase)
expected_results: 50 and has_more true; 10 and has_more false; the clamp returns at most 200

test_cases.name: ack is monotonic and refuses foreign or impossible positions (DataCase)
preconditions: H with DMs at seq 1..3; S2 held by another holder
steps: ack a batch of dm seq 3 and S2 seq 1
expected_results: last_seq 2, still 2; {:error, {:ack_beyond_end, :dm, H.id}}; {:error, {:not_in_inbox, :story, S2.id}}; the batch is refused whole and last_seq stays 2

test_cases.name: a takeover reads the whole thread once (DataCase)
preconditions: S1 held by H1 with 4 messages, H1 acked all; H1 unclaims; H2 claims S1 (Progress.claim_story/3 with H2's credential)
expected_results: 4 messages; then none; H1's last_seq still 4

test_cases.name: routes need a holder credential (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder credential; plain agent key; orchestrator key; user key
steps: GET /api/v1/inbox and POST /api/v1/inbox/ack with each key
expected_results: holder credential 200 with dms/threads/channel; the others 403 holder_credential_required

test_cases.name: inbox tool posts acks before reading
preconditions: mcp-server with a stubbed fetch recording calls
steps: call inbox {project_id, ack: [{kind: "dm", id: h, seq: 3}]}
expected_results: POST /api/v1/inbox/ack then GET /api/v1/inbox?project_id=...; tool declared and dispatched (node --test); description says the cursor moves only on ack

test_cases.name: a message arriving between read and ack is not skipped (DataCase)
expected_results: the second read returns exactly seq 3

test_cases.name: merge drops the source channel's cursors (DataCase)
preconditions: H acked source channel seq 3; source and target projects

test_cases.name: tenant isolation: another tenant's holder sees nothing (DataCase)
preconditions: DMs and a held thread in tenant A; holder HB in tenant B

technical_notes: Name: the table is channel_cursors (README names table), the schema Loopctl.Coordination.InboxCursor, because Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelCursor is already the keyset codec (channel_cursor.ex:1-53) used by recent_page/3.

Ordering: attachment_seq and channel_posts_attachment_seq_uidx are provided by US-52.22; commit order equals attachment_seq order per attachment, so `attachment_seq > last_seq` needs no look-back. The read uses that index per attachment; one query per attachment kind, with the held-story set from stories.assigned_holder_id (provided by US-52.14).
Holder credential: conn.assigns.current_api_key.holder_id (api_keys.holder_id, provided by US-52.13); the plug is a small RequireHolder in lib/loopctl_web/plugs/, used by the inbox controller only.
Inbox messages carry the full body (each at most 16 384 bytes, channel_post.ex:97); the SessionStart and tool-round hooks (US-52.28) render bounded previews themselves.
Excluded from every inbox section: quarantined rows (quarantined_at IS NOT NULL), as every coordination read does today (channel_post.ex:202-212).
Merge: lib/loopctl/projects/merge.ex; channel_cursors has no project_id column, so it is not in @project_tables; the delete runs in the merge transaction.

Routes under the authenticated /api/v1 scope (router.ex:245), operation/2 with 403 holder_credential_required and 422 ack_beyond_end / not_in_inbox; MCP: mcp-server/lib/messages.js (US-52.23) gains the inbox request shape, a declaration and a case in index.js, README row; CHANGELOG.md: new endpoints.
non_goals: Deleting a holder's cursors and DMs when its session ends: US-52.25.
The SessionStart inbox block and the tool-round hook: US-52.28.
A thread history view for fleet_dash: release 5 (README names table: visibility, work_item_timeline).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.24.3 and AC-52.24.6: a cursor moves only on an explicit ack naming a seq the caller received, so a read whose reply is lost in a partition is returned again on reconnect.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.24.1: read positions live in channel_cursors in Postgres, so a session restart or a successor holder reads on from the stored position.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.24.3: ack takes the greater of the stored and acked seq, so a retried or reordered ack never moves a cursor back and never past what was received (AC-52.24.7).
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.24.2: a slow reader gets the same unacked messages again, in order, so slow means late and never lost or skipped.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: inline in the request process; the session reaches its inbox by its holder credential from any machine.

definition_of_done: From an MCP session: inbox returns a DM sent to it by message_send from another session; inbox with that DM's ack then returns no DM; SELECT last_seq FROM channel_cursors WHERE holder_id = <holder> AND attachment_kind = 'dm' equals the DM's attachment_seq.
defaults: Inbox page: 50 messages, clamped to 200 (owner may change).
The channel section is included only when the caller passes project_id (the session's repo project).
